data.title: Daily Shadow Patterns Lab
data.description: Investigate how shadows change in length and direction throughout the day as the sun moves across the sky.

challenges.instruction: Record the shadow data for 8:00 AM by finding its direction and relative length.
challenges.hint: When the sun is low on the horizon in the early morning, think about how stretched out the shadow will be.

challenges.instruction: Record the shadow data for 10:00 AM by finding its direction and relative length.
challenges.hint: As the sun climbs higher in the morning sky, the shadow starts to get shorter.

challenges.instruction: Record the shadow data for 12:00 PM by finding its direction and relative length.
challenges.hint: At midday, when the sun is almost directly overhead, shadows are at their shortest.

challenges.instruction: Record the shadow data for 2:00 PM by finding its direction and relative length.
challenges.hint: Now that the sun has moved past the middle of the sky to the afternoon side, which way does the shadow point?

challenges.instruction: Record the shadow data for 4:00 PM by finding its direction and relative length.
challenges.hint: As evening approaches and the sun gets lower in the west, shadows stretch out again.
